fair_value.method: Blend as of Sep 2027 of forward P/E (50%), EV/sales (25%) and a 5-year FCF DCF (25%): 22x ~$10.2 NTM non-GAAP EPS = $225; 9x ~$4.0B NTM sales plus ~$1.8B net cash = $184; DCF at 11% WACC from a lower $1.5B FY28 FCF base = $230; blended ~$216 on ~205M diluted shares. Down from $220 because net cash and cash conversion were too optimistic in round 1.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM (Q3 FY28-Q2 FY29) non-GAAP EPS ~$10.2 at Sep 2027: FY28 EPS ~$8.8-9.2 (modest haircut to $9.63 consensus, which implies ~+55% FY28 revenue; management guides 'outsized growth again' in FY28), FY29 +25%; multiple 22x (today ~22x FY28 consensus). Held flat, not raised, because peer multiples are compressing (Mizuho cut its target to $245 from $290 on lower peer multiples) and growth decelerates

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: NTM revenue at Sep 2027 ~$4.0B (FY27 ~$2.5B, FY28 ~+50-55%); 9x EV/sales (vs ~11x forward today); net cash ~$1.8B by Sep 2027, down from $2.5B in round 1 (cash+investments $764M after the $735.6M DustPhotonics outlay; Q1 OCF only $90M); 205M diluted shares: (36.0+1.8)/0.205 = ~$184

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FY28 FCF ~$1.5B (cut from $1.6B for inventory/receivables build: Q1 FY27 FCF ~$83M on $236M non-GAAP NI, inventory $313M), then +35%/25%/20%/15%/12%; WACC 11%; terminal growth 4%; PV of FCF plus TV ~$45.4B + net cash ~$1.8B = ~$47.2B / 205M shares

bear.story: The H2 FY27 ramp (~$1.47B needed, ~23% q/q vs ~10% recently) falls short, or the dominant customer (43% of direct billings, 57% of receivables; likely Amazon Trainium) dual-sources 1.6T AECs to Marvell, which is ahead on 3nm retimers and partnered with Amphenol. Opex growth and weak cash conversion compress margins; FY28 EPS is cut to ~$6-6.5 and the multiple de-rates to ~15-16x in an AI-capex digestion.

base.story: FY27 lands near $2.4-2.5B with optical >$600M. FY28 grows ~50% ('outsized growth again', plus first ALC and OmniConnect revenue), a bit under consensus. The stock trades ~22x NTM EPS of ~$10, so it ends roughly flat to modestly up from $211. Cash conversion normalizes once the inventory build unwinds.

bull.story: Amazon Trn3 ramps strongly in 2027 (Mizuho checks), AEC wins broaden across hyperscalers and neoclouds, and 1.6T AEC, optical DSP and DustPhotonics SiPho ramp early. FY28 EPS beats $10.5 and FY29 visibility supports ~27x on ~$12.5-13 NTM EPS, taking the stock past the $308 June 2026 high. Capped a little below round 1 because peer multiples are compressing.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$125 the stock would trade at ~13x FY28 consensus EPS of $9.63 and ~17% below the verified $150.09 closing low of 2026-09-14, itself a sentiment-only selloff after a beat-and-raise. A close there would most likely reflect a genuine estimate reset, not ordinary volatility in a ~90%-vol stock. Candidate causes are a loss, pause or dual-source at the 43%-of-billings customer (e.g. Marvell 1.6T AECs), a failed H2 FY27 ramp with a guide-down, or a hyperscaler capex cut.

key_uncertainties: Whether the steep back-half FY27 ramp (~$1.47B in H2 vs ~$1.01B in H1) materializes
Customer concentration: top two end customers 61%, top four 84%; one direct customer is 43% of revenue and 57% of receivables
Marvell competition in 1.6T AEC retimers (ahead on 3nm, partnered with Amphenol, reportedly priced below Credo)
Cash conversion: Q1 OCF $90M and FCF ~$83M against $236M non-GAAP NI because of inventory and receivables build
Pace of CPO/optical displacement of copper AECs at 1.6T and beyond vs Credo's own optical ramp
AI capex cycle durability, compressing peer multiples and the stock's extreme beta (96% realized vol, -52% peak-to-trough in 2026)
reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's fact-checks, which I verified, changed three inputs. (1) Net cash: cash plus investments is only $764M after the $735.6M DustPhotonics outlay, and Q1 FY27 OCF was $90.2M (FCF ~$83M) against $236M non-GAAP NI because inventory rose to $313M. I cut Sep-2027 net cash from $2.5B to ~$1.8B and FY28 FCF from $1.6B to $1.5B, which lowers EV/sales from $188 to $184 and the DCF from $245 to $230. (2) FY28 growth: management expects 'outsized growth again' in FY28, and $9.63 consensus EPS implies ~+55% revenue. That supports my round-1 +45-55% path, so the P/E leg stays at $225 (22x ~$10.2). I do not raise the multiple, because Mizuho cut its target to $245 on lower peer multiples. (3) Concentration is worse than I stated: one direct customer is 43% of revenue and 57% of receivables, and Marvell is ahead on 1.6T AEC retimers. That argues for keeping my fat left tail (P(<$127) ~25%, slightly more than the supervisor's ~21%, which I think is too thin given a single-customer sourcing decision can cut revenue by a third). On the right tail, my round-1 P(>=$527) of 0.11 was the highest of the panel. With multiples compressing and cash conversion weak, I trimmed the right tail (P(>=$527) 0.08, P(>=$422) 0.15, P(>=$369) 0.21). I kept it above the panel mean because the stock went $86 to $309 inside 12 months. Blended fair value is $216 vs $211 spot, so the median sits at ~$211 (P>=$211 = 0.50), with modest earnings-driven drift offset by de-rating risk. Width reflects an effective ~70-75% lognormal sigma with a slightly fatter left tail: well below the 96% realized vol (inflated by event gaps) but far above the 25-35% large-cap base rate. The scenario mix (25% $100 / 50% $220 / 25% $345; mean ~$221) is consistent with the ladder. No option data or priors were consulted.
